At a regular partnership meeting, discuss the pending activation decision and the work or concerns affecting it. The partnership, its members, and participating advisory groups can do this repeatedly.

A member, the regional health network, or the community group raises a local concern for discussion at a partnership meeting. The concern may slow meeting progress until addressed; the existing concern-resolution actions can address it.

A member country reviews and works on its own readiness for deployment, reporting outstanding requirements or updated readiness findings. Any member country may repeat this work as circumstances change.
The regional health network tests and improves cross-border system interoperability, reporting remaining issues or updated results. It may repeat this work as the system changes.

The partnership coordinates practical preparations for activation across members and tracks what remains before deployment can proceed. It may repeat this work as requirements or circumstances change.
The technical group assesses the system, tests its operation, and reports or works on technical gaps that affect deployment readiness. It may repeat the assessment as changes are made.
The legal group reviews the legal and regulatory requirements for activation and reports or works on remaining gaps. It may repeat the review as requirements or arrangements change.
The logistics group develops and updates the operational plan for deployment, working on gaps that could prevent or delay activation. It may repeat this work as plans and circumstances change.

The community group consults local communities, conveys their perspective, and works with the partnership on practical local issues affecting deployment. It may repeat this work as concerns or plans change.
